name: cranfield-1400

source.host: University of Glasgow IR group test collections

redistribution.reason: The collection has no published license, so no part of it is committed to this repository. The evaluation runner downloads the archive at run time into target/ and verifies it against archive_sha256 and archive_bytes before use.

citation: Cleverdon, C. W. (1967). The Cranfield tests on index language devices. Aslib Proceedings 19(6), 173-194. The 1,400-abstract, 225-query collection with graded judgments is the Cranfield 2 test collection distributed by the SMART and Glasgow IR resources.

conventions.document_ids: The text after '.I ' on a document's header line, as a string ('1' to '1400'). Cassie _id is that string, so ties order lexicographically ('10' before '2').
conventions.indexed_text: title + ' ' + text (the .T and .W fields), the ir_datasets default_text convention. The abstract usually restates the title, so title terms count twice; this is kept so results are comparable with published ir_datasets baselines.
conventions.query_numbering: A query's identity is its 1-based sequential position in cran.qry. The '.I' numbers in cran.qry skip values (001, 002, 004, 008, ...) and are NOT the numbers used by cranqrel.
conventions.qrel_format: Three whitespace-separated columns per line: query position, document id, relevance level. Any other column count is an error.

relevance_levels.1: References which are a complete answer to the question.
relevance_levels.2: References of a high degree of relevance, the lack of which either would have made the research impracticable or would have resulted in a considerable amount of extra work.
relevance_levels.3: References which were useful, either as general background to the work or as suggesting methods of tackling certain aspects of the work.
relevance_levels.4: References of minimum interest, for example, those that have been included from an historical viewpoint.
relevance_levels.-1: References of no interest (Cleverdon's level 5, recoded as -1 in the file).

conventions.relevance_level_note: The definitions above are Cleverdon's, from cranqrel.readme shipped in the archive: level 1 is the strongest. ir_datasets v0.5.11 labels level 4 as the complete answer in QREL_DEFS, which contradicts the readme and the level frequencies (level 1 is rarest at 128 judgments, level 3 most common at 734); this evaluation follows the readme. ir_datasets passes the numeric levels through unchanged, so only its labels differ.
conventions.grade_rationale: Grade is 5 minus the level for levels 1 to 4, so a larger grade is always more relevant; level -1 (no interest) is grade 0, the same as an unjudged document. nDCG@10 uses gain 2^grade - 1, the repository's existing definition, so a complete answer (15) is worth 15 times a historical reference (1).
conventions.mrr_rationale: MRR@10 counts a document as relevant at grade 2 or above, levels 1 to 3 (complete answer, high relevance, useful background). Level 4 is historical interest only and does not count, which matches the repository's relevance threshold for the in-tree workload.

evaluation.analyzer: Each configuration's analyzer: standard tokenizer (split on non-alphanumeric characters), case folding, English stop words, no synonyms; stemming as listed per configuration.
evaluation.sql: SELECT _id, search_score(body, $1) AS score FROM docs WHERE search(body, $1) ORDER BY score DESC, _id ASC LIMIT 10

bm25.statistics: Corpus-wide: document count, document frequency and average analyzed length cover all 1,400 documents. Score is the sum over distinct query terms of idf * tf * (k1 + 1) / (tf + k1 * (1 - b + b * length / average)), with idf = ln((N - df + 0.5) / (df + 0.5) + 1).

evaluation.contract: Tier 1 (correctness, hard gate): for every configuration, Cassie must match the independent BM25 reference on every Cranfield query: identical top-10 document ids in identical order, and each score within score_tolerance. Tier 2 (no regression): each configuration's mean nDCG@10 and MRR@10 must be at least its pinned min_mean_ndcg_at_10 and min_mean_mrr_at_10, set 0.005 below the first measured value. Tier 3 (quality): the english_stemming configuration must score at least the default configuration on both means. No absolute 0.80 floor applies to Cranfield: exact BM25 scores far below it on this collection, so such a floor would measure the collection, not Cassie.
